divergences.old: File arguments (--input-file, --jql-file, --fields-file, --file, --dir, @file values) reading or writing any path the OS user can reach
divergences.toil: A path outside the workspace (--workspace, TOIL_WORKSPACE, the CLI's working directory, or the MCP client's single root) is refused with INVALID_INPUT, after resolving .., symlinks and junctions; relative paths resolve against the workspace. A user can lift this one with "bounds": { "files": "unbounded" } in their config (docs/bounds.md)
divergences.why: A path an agent passes, perhaps from a prompt in an issue, must not reach files the user never pointed toil at.

divergences.old: File arguments (--input-file, --jql-file, --fields-file, --file, --dir, @file values) reading or writing any path
divergences.toil: A path at or under ~/.toil/ or the --config file, or under /proc/ or /sys/, is refused with INVALID_INPUT, after resolving .., symlinks and junctions
divergences.why: A path an agent passes must not turn a read into a way to send toil's config or the environment's tokens to a service's host.

divergences.old: Global --output-file replacing a file that already exists, or writing toil's own files or under /proc or /sys
divergences.toil: Refused with INVALID_INPUT, and the error envelope goes to stdout with exit code 1; the existing file is left alone. It may still write outside the workspace (docs/bounds.md, output-file)
divergences.why: An agent driving the CLI must not be able to overwrite toil's config, or any file, with an envelope.

divergences.toil: Removed. Run the command without --allow-write, which refuses the write
divergences.why: It could only intercept writes made over HTTP, showed only the first of several, and saw little use. Writes are governed by the two-step gate (writes enabled in config plus --allow-write) alone.

divergences.old: An id, key or name of . or .. pasted into a request path, which URL normalisation collapsed, so the request (a write included) reached a different endpoint on the same host
divergences.toil: A request path with a . or .. segment (or %2e spellings of one) is refused with INVALID_INPUT naming the segment, before anything is sent. Dots inside a segment (v1.2) are unchanged
divergences.why: A value an agent passes must not redirect a command, or its credential, to an endpoint the command doesn't name (docs/bounds.md, requests.path).
